## Headline lifespan figures (standard lab conditions, from each doc's "Headline")
| Organism | Median lifespan | Appendix table |
|---|---|---|
| C. elegans | 18 days | A-7 |
| D. melanogaster | 60 days | A-3 |
| S. cerevisiae | 25 divisions (replicative, not calendar time) | A-9 |
| N. furzeri (killifish) | 16 weeks | A-2 |
| M. musculus | 30 months | A-5 |
| D. rerio | 42 months | A-4 |

In calendar time, killifish (about 4 months) is the shortest-lived vertebrate. C. elegans (about 2.5 weeks) and Drosophila (about 2 months) are the shortest-lived animals overall. Mouse (about 2.5 years) and zebrafish (about 3.5 years) are the longest-lived. Yeast is measured in divisions, so it cannot be compared directly.

## Cohort-level "Discussion" data (not individually transcribed)
Each doc has several hundred cohort entries, in the form "median survival was X% of controls (n=…, intervention, lab #)". They are not listed here. They have these features:
- Interventions are dietary restriction, heat stress, metformin, rapamycin and daf-2 RNAi.
- Values range roughly 40% to 160% of controls in every organism.
- Sample sizes range roughly n=20 to n=400, across labs 1–40.
- There is no obvious consistent directional effect per intervention in any organism. The values look very noisy, and the same cohort ID often appears several times with different values.
- Data-quality flag: daf-2 RNAi appears as an intervention in yeast, mouse, zebrafish, Drosophila and killifish. This is biologically odd, for example because yeast has no daf-2 ortholog. Treat the cohort-level data cautiously.
- The reviews give no explicit throughput data. Throughput (generation time, cohort size, housing) has to be inferred from the lifespan figures and from what the appendix housing units imply. The synthesis should say this explicitly.
